# ORB Dynamics

> ORB Dynamics develops autonomous, long-endurance hydrogen airships for persistent aerial watch. The design target is 24 hours or more on station per flight and a range of 1,000-2,000 km, powered by hydrogen fuel cells whose only exhaust is water. Incubated at YES!Delft, with research from TU Delft.

## What the airship does

- Wildfire detection: early alerts for fire crews, from an airship that stays over the area instead of landing to refuel.
- Infrastructure and government: patrol of powerlines, pipelines, rail and maritime areas.
- Cargo transport: autonomous middle-mile freight.

## Why an airship

Drones and helicopters must land to refuel, and helicopters burn kerosene. Manufacturer figures for time aloft per flight:

- Multirotor drone (DJI Matrice 350 RTK): about 35 minutes with a gimbal camera fitted.
- Fixed-wing drone (Quantum Systems Vector AI): about 3 hours.
- Light helicopter (Airbus H125): about 4.5 hours.
- ORB airship: 24 hours or more (design target, not yet flown).

The ORB airship is in development. Endurance and range are design targets, not measured performance.

## Simulation

An illustrative simulation shows six ORB airships patrolling Ourense, Spain, on real terrain and detecting two wildfires. Detection probabilities in it are model approximations, not measured performance. Video: https://orbdynamics.eu/img/orb-sim.mp4
